governanceNotes: D1 batch 66 (2026-09-26): two bounded association edges authored - orthostatic-hypotension to dizziness (rank 1) and to cognitive-disorder (rank 2) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The dizziness proposition rests on the Barany Society/ICVD hemodynamic orthostatic dizziness and vertigo diagnostic criteria requiring documented orthostatic blood pressure failure and attributing symptoms to global brain hypoperfusion (PMID 30883381). The cognitive-disorder proposition rests on the cross-posture systematic review (eight studies; cognition worse upright across multiple domains; PMID 42732657) and the older-adult orthostatic-disorder perspective (impaired cardiovascular-cerebral reserve framing; PMID 42740891).

Counter-evidence and caveat screens recorded 2026-09-26: (i) constitutive boundary - orthostatic hypotension is defined hemodynamically and may be asymptomatic, so dizziness is carried as a consequence phenotype with the ICVD criteria requiring documented blood pressure failure to exclude vestibular mimics; (ii) state-versus-trait - the cognitive edge carries acute posture-dependent decrement openly and supports chronic-disorder framing only at perspective level; (iii) shared substrate - Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple system atrophy, and cerebrovascular disease produce both orthostatic hypotension and cognitive decline, so the shared-substrate alternative is primary among exclusions; (iv) withheld propositions - falls (no catalog identity despite dominant clinical burden), hemodynamic syncope (vasovagal-syncope is a reflex entity; generic syncope has no identity), and orthostatic visual blurring (transient hypoperfusion, ME-29 sibling-window discipline with the published hypotension visual-impairment window); (v) evidence-class discipline - the dizziness anchor is a consensus criteria document without incidence quantification and the cognitive anchor set is eight small cross-posture studies per the authors' own limitations.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Orthostatic hypotension is the documented hemodynamic substrate of orthostatic dizziness at international-consensus diagnostic-criteria level: the Barany Society and ICVD diagnostic criteria for hemodynamic orthostatic dizziness and vertigo, derived by expert consensus from an extensive review of 90 years of research, require five or more episodes of dizziness, unsteadiness, or vertigo triggered by arising or present during upright position and subsiding with sitting or lying down together with orthostatic hypotension, postural tachycardia syndrome, or syncope documented on standing or head-up tilt, explicitly attributing the symptom to global brain hypoperfusion and distinguishing it from other etiologies (PMID 30883381); recorded as documented association only with the constitutive-boundary screen carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: orthostatic hypotension is defined hemodynamically (a blood pressure fall on standing) and can be fully asymptomatic, so dizziness is a consequence phenotype rather than a defining feature, and individual claims require dated supine-to-standing blood pressure documentation with vestibular, medication, and arrhythmic exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Cerebral hypoperfusion on standing from impaired blood pressure autoregulation drives transient global brain hypoperfusion so orthostatic dizziness and unsteadiness result, the hypoperfusion route explicitly named in the consensus criteria (hemodynamic orthostatic dizziness distinguished from other etiologies by documented orthostatic blood pressure failure), but whether this route produced any individual dizziness remains hypothesized until tilt-table and ambulatory records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at international consensus diagnostic-criteria class only: the anchor is an expert-consensus criteria document rather than a quantifying cohort, so no incidence or relative risk is carried from it, and the criteria deliberately require documented orthostatic blood pressure failure to exclude vestibular and other causes, meaning the association is definitional-adjacent and boundary discipline is carried openly.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The anchor is a consensus criteria document without incidence quantification; the criteria themselves acknowledge postural tachycardia syndrome and syncope as alternative documented hemodynamic substrates; orthostatic dizziness is common in older adults with multifactorial attribution; and vestibular disorders (benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, vestibular migraine), anemia, medication-induced orthostasis, arrhythmia, and presyncope versus true vertigo distinctions compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: postural tachycardia syndrome as a distinct documented substrate (the ICVD criteria name it separately)

evidenceGaps: The anchor is a consensus criteria document without incidence quantification; the criteria themselves acknowledge postural tachycardia syndrome and syncope as alternative documented hemodynamic substrates; orthostatic dizziness is common in older adults with multifactorial attribution; and vestibular disorders (benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, vestibular migraine), anemia, medication-induced orthostasis, arrhythmia, and presyncope versus true vertigo distinctions compete for individual attribution.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at international-consensus-diagnostic-criteria class with the definitional-boundary limit carried openly: the ICVD hemodynamic orthostatic dizziness and vertigo criteria, derived from 90 years of research by expert consensus, require positional dizziness episodes plus documented orthostatic hypotension, postural tachycardia syndrome, or syncope and explicitly attribute the symptom to global brain hypoperfusion (PMID 30883381); because the anchor is a criteria document without incidence quantification and orthostatic hypotension itself can be asymptomatic, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated supine-to-standing blood pressure measurement with vestibular, anemic, medication, and arrhythmic exclusion.

sourceReferences.citation: Kim HA, Bisdorff A, Bronstein AM, et al. Hemodynamic orthostatic dizziness/vertigo: Diagnostic criteria J Vestib Res. 2019;29(2-3):45-56. PMID 30883381.
sourceReferences.note: Barany Society / ICVD diagnostic criteria for hemodynamic orthostatic dizziness/vertigo (J Vestib Res 2019; expert consensus from extensive review of 90 years of research): definite criteria require >= 5 episodes of dizziness/unsteadiness/vertigo triggered by arising or upright posture subsiding with sitting/lying, plus orthostatic hypotension, POTS, or syncope documented on standing or head-up tilt, and no better account; symptom attributed to global brain hypoperfusion; probable criteria add accompanying blurred vision, difficulty thinking, weakness, or tachycardia; supports the bounded hypoperfusion-symptom association only.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Orthostatic hypotension documents cognitive impairment at systematic-review and clinical-perspective level: the systematic review of upright posture effects on cognition in orthostatic hypotension (PROSPERO CRD42025649093; eight studies with cognitive testing in both postures) found cognitive function significantly worse upright than supine across global function, attention and processing speed, executive function, language, memory and learning, and visuospatial domains (PMID 42732657), and the clinical perspective on orthostatic blood pressure disorders in older adults frames these disorders as markers of impaired cardiovascular-cerebral reserve with implications for cerebral perfusion, cognition, and functional status and potential to reduce falls and cognitive complications with recognition (PMID 42740891); recorded as documented association only with the state-versus-trait boundary carried openly.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual: the systematic review establishes posture-dependent cognitive decrement (state) rather than a diagnosed persistent cognitive disorder (trait), the chronic-disorder framing is supported at perspective level only, and shared neurodegenerative substrates (Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple system atrophy) cause both orthostatic hypotension and cognitive decline, so individual claims require dated neuropsychological assessment with neurodegenerative, vascular, and medication exclusion.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Repeated and sustained cerebral hypoperfusion during upright posture drives transient cognitive performance decrements and, hypothesized over longer exposure, increased vulnerability to cognitive decline so cognitive impairment results, the hypoperfusion route supported by the cross-posture cognitive differences in the systematic review and the cardiovascular-cerebral reserve framing of the perspective, but whether this route produced any individual cognitive disorder remains hypothesized until neuropsychological and hemodynamic records are reviewed.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association is supported at systematic review of eight cross-posture studies plus clinical-perspective class only: the review quantifies acute posture-dependent performance differences rather than incident cognitive disorder, study methods varied (tilt angles, durations, ambulation, statistics) per the authors' own limitations, and no longitudinal cohort quantifying dementia incidence in orthostatic hypotension was located in this pass.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The systematic review establishes acute upright cognitive decrement only, with the authors flagging heterogeneous tilt angles, durations, ambulation restrictions, and statistical methods across the eight studies; no longitudinal incident-dementia quantification was located in this pass; shared-substrate confounding is substantial (Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple system atrophy, and cerebrovascular disease produce both orthostatic hypotension and cognitive decline); medication burden (anticholinergics, sedatives, polypharmacy) is pervasive in affected populations; and depression, delirium, sleep disorders, and sensory impairment compete for individual attribution.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: shared neurodegenerative substrate (Parkinson disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, multiple system atrophy - both orthostatic hypotension and cognitive decline are manifestations)
